proves.claim: shardJobs returns exactly one gate's shard rows in order, never a sibling gate's, and its query searches the job_id key instead of scanning every job row.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-key-range.why: Without this test shardJobs can slide back to a substr scan of every gate-shard row on each pull claim, so claim cost grows with the number of gates.

proves.claim: On a board of 20000 gate-shard rows across 500 gates, a settleDoneShardGates pass over 30 candidate gates takes under 5 ms, its time printed.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-scale.why: Without this measurement a slide back to a full scan of the shard rows would only show as a slow pull claim on the live board.

proves.claim: On 20000 gate-shard rows across 500 gates shardJobs returns each gate's shards exactly as the old substr query did, and its query searches the job primary-key index, not job_kind_created.

api.io-gate.shard-jobs-key-range-scale.why: Without this test a planner change could move shardJobs back onto job_kind_created, which reads every gate-shard row on each pull claim on the live board.
